KEY MESSAGE 1...
Scattered showers have lifted into the area ahead of a complex
low pressure system to the south. This system currently has two
low pressure centers with one approx. 275nm SE of Cape Hatteras
with a second weaker low just east of Jacksonville, FL. Both
lows will lift north with the stronger low passing about 100nm 
east of the OBX this afternoon while the second low weakens as 
it approaches ENC. 

The greatest impacts with this system continue to be felt along
the coast where large surf, beach erosion, and minor ocean 
overwash will be possible with the contribution of high
astronomical tides adding to the impacts. Have not received any
reports of overwash as of yet but will continue the Coastal
Flood Advisory for Hatteras Island coinciding with the highest
seas and this morning's high tide cycle. Any potential minor 
ocean overwash would be relegated to the most vulnerable dune 
structures along Hwy 12 on Hatteras Island. Coastal flooding 
impacts across the sounds and rivers will be minimal at best 
giving the weaker winds, but given the developing King Tides, 
there may be minor inundation for locations adjacent to the 
sounds and rivers. Will also continue the High Surf Advisory 
for Core Banks up through Hatteras Island and also expand it to
include the Northern Outer Banks where waves in the surf zone
are expected to be as high as 8-10ft. 

Rainfall amounts continue to be underwhelming as ENC looks to 
remain between the two areas of ascent with much of ENC now only
forecast to see 0.25-0.75" of rain with this system.. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...We enter a King Tide Cycle today which will 
continue through the week, peaking during the middle of the 
week. This higher than normal astronomical tide cycle is 
slightly stronger than the one that occurred the last week of 
OCT. The tide levels may be exacerbated by a series of low 
pressure systems that are expected to impact the region over the
next week. 

The first system lifting across the area today continues to
under perform in regards to the winds and not expecting any 
impacts across the sounds and rivers. However, this system is 
producing large surf along the coast and the higher than normal 
tides may help contribute to some minor ocean overwash around 
times of high tide, especially where the dune structure is 
compromised along Hatteras Island.

Another stronger low pressure system is expected to impact the 
area around the middle of next week. The strength and track of 
this low will determine where the greatest impacts will occur, 
but most tidal locations across ENC should expect elevated water
levels with at least minor to moderate impacts across the 
typical vulnerable areas. Interests along the coast should watch
the forecast closely over the next week for the potential for 
greater impacts, especially as it has to potential to impact 
holiday travel.

KEY MESSAGE 3...
Strong high pressure building across the Great Lakes and 
northern mid Atlantic will ridge southward into the area Tuesday
into Wednesday. Meanwhile, a deepening upper level trough moves
through the Gulf states and progresses offshore of the SE US 
with a surface low developing along the coast or just off the 
coast near the Gulf Stream. This low then deepens as it lifts 
northward off the coast Wednesday into Thursday. Upper level 
support is greater with this system and high pressure to the 
north will be stronger which will likely bring a tighter 
pressure gradient across the area resulting in stronger winds. 
While there remains uncertainty with the exact details with this
system, it will have the potential to bring greater impacts 
across the area, especially along the coast and tidal locations 
as it will coincide with the peak of King Tides bringing a 
greater risk of coastal flooding, beach erosion, and ocean 
overwash. This system will also have the potential to bring very
strong winds and periods of heavy rain which will likely impact
holiday travel on Wednesday and Thursday.
